raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #5317.

## Why

The controller, the rollouter, the trainer, the batcher and `train.py` used Monarch directly: `train.py` provisioned the GPU proc meshes; the controller spawned the router and batcher processes, set up torch elastic, spawned every actor, sliced the trainer by DP rank and stopped the meshes; the rollouter spawned and stopped its worker pool; the batcher and the trainer exchanged `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch`es. Running the RL loop on another actor framework (e.g. Ray) would mean editing all of them.

This PR puts actor placement behind an interface selected by config, the way `Generator.Config.engine` selects the inference engine (#5317).

## What changed

- **`actors/system.py`: `ActorSystem`**, framework-agnostic. It provisions processes, spawns each service, initializes TorchStore (storage on the trainer's processes, plus every trainer and generator actor's client), stops the processes, and shuts its client down. The name follows Akka/Pekko's actor system (see its docstring). Its docstring also defines the call convention its handles follow: `.call()` with `.get(rank)` on the result, `.call_one()`, `.choose()`, `.stream()`, `.broadcast()` (Monarch's endpoint calls; another framework wraps its handles to provide them).
  - `spawn_trainer(config, dp_degree=...)` returns a **`TrainerHandle`**: all-ranks, rank-0 and per-DP-rank handles. The actor system slices the trainer by DP rank and checks the `(dp, cp, tp)` layout with `get_dp_rank`, so the controller no longer slices meshes.
  - `spawn_generator_router(router_config, generator_config=...)` spawns the generators and the router over them, and returns only the router: the controller reaches the generators through the router.
  - `spawn_batcher`, `spawn_rollout_workers` / `stop_rollout_workers`.
- **`Controller.Config.actor_system`** selects the implementation; the default `MonarchActorSystem.Config()` is imported lazily. `Controller.setup_async(actor_system=...)` also accepts one the launcher built, e.g. a `MonarchActorSystem` on hosts it allocated (`host_meshes`, `generator_env` constructor arguments), so launchers that bring their own hosts keep working. `train.py` only builds, runs and closes the controller, then calls the actor system's `shutdown()`.
- **`actors/monarch/system.py`: `MonarchActorSystem`.** `actors/monarch/provisioning.py` takes `train.py`'s proc mesh provisioning (`PerHostProvisioner`, `HostMeshes`, `spawn_proc_mesh`, the spawn bootstraps) plus `spawn_cpu_procs` and the client `shutdown`.
- **`actors/monarch/router.py`: `InterGeneratorRouterActor`**, the endpoints and the singleton check. `InterGeneratorRouter` is now a plain class with public async methods, like `Trainer` and `Generator`.
- **RDMA microbatches (separate commit).** `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch` moves to `actors/monarch/rdma_microbatch.py`. The batcher and the trainer use an `RDMAMicrobatch` protocol (`read`, `drop`, the batch/DP rank/microbatch indices) in `trainer/rdma_microbatch.py`, next to `RDMAMicrobatchPrefetcher`; `BatcherActor` injects `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch.register` into `Batcher`.
- **Fix:** `VerifiersRollouter.setup_async` takes `actor_system` (unused: rollouts run in the Verifiers EnvServer), plus a test that its signature matches `Rollouter.setup_async`.

After this PR no module outside `actors/monarch/` imports Monarch, except the controller's lazy default config. `actors/monarch/README.md` describes the package and the call convention that remains outside it.

## Behavior

- Processes and actors are created in the same order as before: GPU meshes, router and batcher processes, torch elastic, trainer, generators, router, batcher, rollout workers, TorchStore. The trainer's DP-rank layout check now runs right after the trainer spawns instead of after TorchStore init. Teardown order is unchanged.
- `ts.initialize(mesh=trainer_mesh)` and the per-actor TorchStore client setup move into `ActorSystem.initialize_torchstore()` (with a TODO to move it to a model state dict transport).
- A batcher with `rdma_min_tensor_bytes` set but no registration raises `ValueError`.

## Testing

- RL CPU unit tests: 497 passed, 8 skipped. The Verifiers tests (skipped without `verifiers`) pass with `verifiers==0.3.1`: 37 passed, 1 skipped. New tests cover provisioning order and launcher host meshes, trainer DP-rank grouping and the layout check, teardown order with the batcher, and the Batcher's missing-registration error.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: clean.
- GPU A/B against main (`dc9ea005e`), GB300, Qwen3 debug model with random init and a deterministic varying reward, 6 steps:
  - on-policy, batch-invariant, 1 trainer GPU + 1 generator GPU: all non-timing metrics bitwise identical (only time-to-first-token differs);
  - same, with a DP=2 trainer and `rdma_min_tensor_bytes=1024` (3 GPUs, per-DP-rank columns over RDMA): bitwise identical;
  - async (`target_offpolicy_steps=3`): finishes all steps on both. Both then hit the same teardown error on main and here (the rollout worker mesh stops while a router reply is in flight).

nodes.body: The dependency inversion itself makes sense if the goal is to support multiple backends. But it does come with a price since it requires more work when the interface gets complicated. e.g. https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5285 would need more careful design to conform with the `ActorSystem` interface.

message from claude:

@tianyu-l one concern before this merges: launchers that bring their own hosts.

1. On main, `Controller.setup_async(trainer_mesh=..., generator_meshes=...)` lets a launcher allocate hosts itself and hand the controller ready proc meshes.
2. FairTitan's Slurm launcher depends on that. It loads host meshes from its Slurm allocation, calls `spawn_proc_mesh(..., host_meshes=host_meshes, generator_env=...)`, and passes the result to `setup_async`: [launcher/rl/main.py#L49-L60](https://github.com/fairinternal/fairtitan/blob/46a9a467ed6d2524910ba98b0081a8789e6ae947/launcher/rl/main.py#L49-L60) (internal repo).
3. In this PR, `setup_async()` takes no meshes, and `MonarchActorSystem.provision` always calls `spawn_proc_mesh(..., host_meshes=None)` (`torchtitan/rl/actors/monarch/system.py:69`). `spawn_proc_mesh` still accepts `host_meshes`, but nothing can pass them in, so that launcher breaks.

Could `MonarchActorSystem` keep a way to take caller-provided `HostMeshes`, for example a constructor argument or an overridable `provision`? Happy to send it as a follow-up if you'd rather land this as is.

@felipemello1 thanks for catching this, fixed in this PR. `MonarchActorSystem` takes `host_meshes` and `generator_env` constructor arguments, which it passes to `spawn_proc_mesh`, and `Controller.setup_async(actor_system=...)` accepts a system the launcher built:

```python
actor_system = config.actor_system.build(host_meshes=host_meshes, generator_env=generator_env)
await controller.setup_async(actor_system=actor_system)
```

`setup_async()` with no argument builds `config.actor_system` as before. A unit test checks that `provision` passes both through to `spawn_proc_mesh`.
This interface can be remove. Controller only needs `spawn_generator_router` to get the generation stack.

I kept these, because the pool is an implementation detail of the default `Rollouter`: `VerifiersRollouter` runs rollouts in its Verifiers EnvServer and spawns no pool. If the controller spawned the pool and passed it in, it would spawn processes the Verifiers rollouter never uses, or need a "does this rollouter want a pool" flag. So the rollouter still spawns its pool through the actor system it is given.

While checking this I found that `VerifiersRollouter.setup_async` did not take `actor_system`, so the verifiers recipes would have failed. Fixed, with a test that its signature matches `Rollouter.setup_async`. Happy to switch to a controller-owned pool if you prefer it.

detail.body:
Stacked on #5317.

## Why

The controller, the rollouter, the trainer, the batcher and `train.py` used Monarch directly: `train.py` provisioned the GPU proc meshes; the controller spawned the router and batcher processes, set up torch elastic, spawned every actor, sliced the trainer by DP rank and stopped the meshes; the rollouter spawned and stopped its worker pool; the batcher and the trainer exchanged `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch`es. Running the RL loop on another actor framework (e.g. Ray) would mean editing all of them.

This PR puts actor placement behind an interface selected by config, the way `Generator.Config.engine` selects the inference engine (#5317).

## What changed

- **`actors/system.py`: `ActorSystem`**, framework-agnostic. It provisions processes, spawns each service, initializes TorchStore (storage on the trainer's processes, plus every trainer and generator actor's client), stops the processes, and shuts its client down. The name follows Akka/Pekko's actor system (see its docstring). Its docstring also defines the call convention its handles follow: `.call()` with `.get(rank)` on the result, `.call_one()`, `.choose()`, `.stream()`, `.broadcast()` (Monarch's endpoint calls; another framework wraps its handles to provide them).
  - `spawn_trainer(config, dp_degree=...)` returns a **`TrainerHandle`**: all-ranks, rank-0 and per-DP-rank handles. The actor system slices the trainer by DP rank and checks the `(dp, cp, tp)` layout with `get_dp_rank`, so the controller no longer slices meshes.
  - `spawn_generator_router(router_config, generator_config=...)` spawns the generators and the router over them, and returns only the router: the controller reaches the generators through the router.
  - `spawn_batcher`, `spawn_rollout_workers` / `stop_rollout_workers`.
- **`Controller.Config.actor_system`** selects the implementation; the default `MonarchActorSystem.Config()` is imported lazily. `Controller.setup_async(actor_system=...)` also accepts one the launcher built, e.g. a `MonarchActorSystem` on hosts it allocated (`host_meshes`, `generator_env` constructor arguments), so launchers that bring their own hosts keep working. `train.py` only builds, runs and closes the controller, then calls the actor system's `shutdown()`.
- **`actors/monarch/system.py`: `MonarchActorSystem`.** `actors/monarch/provisioning.py` takes `train.py`'s proc mesh provisioning (`PerHostProvisioner`, `HostMeshes`, `spawn_proc_mesh`, the spawn bootstraps) plus `spawn_cpu_procs` and the client `shutdown`.
- **`actors/monarch/router.py`: `InterGeneratorRouterActor`**, the endpoints and the singleton check. `InterGeneratorRouter` is now a plain class with public async methods, like `Trainer` and `Generator`.
- **RDMA microbatches (separate commit).** `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch` moves to `actors/monarch/rdma_microbatch.py`. The batcher and the trainer use an `RDMAMicrobatch` protocol (`read`, `drop`, the batch/DP rank/microbatch indices) in `trainer/rdma_microbatch.py`, next to `RDMAMicrobatchPrefetcher`; `BatcherActor` injects `MonarchRDMAMicrobatch.register` into `Batcher`.
- **Fix:** `VerifiersRollouter.setup_async` takes `actor_system` (unused: rollouts run in the Verifiers EnvServer), plus a test that its signature matches `Rollouter.setup_async`.

After this PR no module outside `actors/monarch/` imports Monarch, except the controller's lazy default config. `actors/monarch/README.md` describes the package and the call convention that remains outside it.

## Behavior

- Processes and actors are created in the same order as before: GPU meshes, router and batcher processes, torch elastic, trainer, generators, router, batcher, rollout workers, TorchStore. The trainer's DP-rank layout check now runs right after the trainer spawns instead of after TorchStore init. Teardown order is unchanged.
- `ts.initialize(mesh=trainer_mesh)` and the per-actor TorchStore client setup move into `ActorSystem.initialize_torchstore()` (with a TODO to move it to a model state dict transport).
- A batcher with `rdma_min_tensor_bytes` set but no registration raises `ValueError`.

## Testing

- RL CPU unit tests: 497 passed, 8 skipped. The Verifiers tests (skipped without `verifiers`) pass with `verifiers==0.3.1`: 37 passed, 1 skipped. New tests cover provisioning order and launcher host meshes, trainer DP-rank grouping and the layout check, teardown order with the batcher, and the Batcher's missing-registration error.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: clean.
- GPU A/B against main (`dc9ea005e`), GB300, Qwen3 debug model with random init and a deterministic varying reward, 6 steps:
  - on-policy, batch-invariant, 1 trainer GPU + 1 generator GPU: all non-timing metrics bitwise identical (only time-to-first-token differs);
  - same, with a DP=2 trainer and `rdma_min_tensor_bytes=1024` (3 GPUs, per-DP-rank columns over RDMA): bitwise identical;
  - async (`target_offpolicy_steps=3`): finishes all steps on both. Both then hit the same teardown error on main and here (the rollout worker mesh stops while a router reply is in flight).

+    """``bootstrap`` setup callable for Generator."""
+    import os
+
+    # TODO: this can be removed if it is addressed upstream in: https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/issues/55
+    # Generator encounters the following issue:
+    # 1. vLLM's jit_monitor transitively imports readline through the following chain:
+    #      vLLM -> tilelang  -> tvm  -> tvm's base.py -> import readline
+    #      https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b23bd73f540175f9e117eaee5029cd7d8df63964/vllm/utils/jit_monitor.py#L451
+    #      https://github.com/tile-ai/tvm/blob/28a0d34420d2fa9bc71fc891445a3f1396fca759/python/tvm/base.py#L71
+    #    readline does tcsetattr on its import, which touches the controlling terminal.
+    # 2. Monarch spawns procs in a background process group.
+    #
+    # As a result, when spawning the Generator mesh, readline-import touches the
+    # controlling terminal in background processes, and kernel sends SIGTTOU, which stops
+    # the process.
+    #
+    # Strictly speaking this should be a tvm bug, since it should not assume the import
+    # happens in a foreground process. To workaround it, we do a proactive readline-import
+    # warmup here with SIGTTOU being temporarily blocked. Then the subsequent readline-import
+    # in tvm will not do tcsetattr again since it is already done here.
+    if os.isatty(0):
+        import signal

+        _prev_mask = signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_BLOCK, {signal.SIGTTOU})
+        try:
+            import readline  # noqa: F401
+        finally:
+            signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_SETMASK, _prev_mask)

+    _preimport_torch()

+
+class PerHostProvisioner:
+    """Allocates non-overlapping GPU ranges within a single host.
+
+    On the same host, the trainer and generator run on separate GPU
+    meshes (e.g. GPUs 0-3 for training, GPUs 4-7 for generation). Each
+    call to `allocate(n)` reserves the next *n* GPUs and returns the launch
+    env (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` plus any `extra_env`) for those GPUs. The
+    returned env vars are applied to the spawned process via ``bootstrap_command``.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, total_gpus: int = 8):
+        self.total_gpus = total_gpus
+        self.next_gpu = 0
+
+    @property
+    def available(self) -> int:
+        return self.total_gpus - self.next_gpu
+
+    def allocate(
+        self, num_gpus: int, *, extra_env: dict[str, str] | None = None
+    ) -> dict[str, str]:
+        if num_gpus > self.available:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Requested {num_gpus} GPUs but only {self.available} "
+                f"available (total={self.total_gpus}, allocated={self.next_gpu})"
+            )
+        gpu_ids = list(range(self.next_gpu, self.next_gpu + num_gpus))
+        self.next_gpu += num_gpus
+
+        env = {"CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": ",".join(str(g) for g in gpu_ids)}
+        if extra_env:
+            env.update(extra_env)
+        return env
+
+
+@dataclass
+class HostMeshes:
+    trainer: HostMesh
+    generators: list[HostMesh]
+    gpus_per_node: int
+
+
+def compute_trainer_world_size(p: ParallelismConfig) -> int:
+    """Compute world size from all parallel dimensions."""
+    dp_shard = max(p.data_parallel_shard_degree, 1)
+    return (
+        p.data_parallel_replicate_degree
+        * dp_shard
+        * p.tensor_parallel_degree
+        * p.pipeline_parallel_degree
+        * p.context_parallel_degree
+    )
+
+
+def compute_generator_world_size(p: InferenceParallelismConfig) -> int:
+    """Number of GPU processes for one generator (vLLM) instance."""
+    return p.data_parallel_degree * p.tensor_parallel_degree
+
+
+def _spawn_proc_mesh(
+    host_mesh: HostMesh,
+    role_world_size: int,
+    provisioner: PerHostProvisioner,
+    *,
+    bootstrap: Callable[[], None],
+    extra_env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+) -> ProcMesh:
+    """Spawn one role's proc mesh on ``host_mesh``, splitting ``role_world_size``
+    evenly across the mesh's hosts. ``extra_env`` is applied in each proc's bootstrap.
+
+    Assumes ``_check_gpus_per_host`` passed: the split is even and the GPUs fit.
+    """
+    nodes = len(host_mesh)
+    role_gpus_per_node = role_world_size // nodes
+    env = provisioner.allocate(role_gpus_per_node, extra_env=extra_env)
+    return host_mesh.spawn_procs(
+        per_host={"gpus": role_gpus_per_node},
+        bootstrap=bootstrap,
+        bootstrap_command=default_bootstrap_cmd().with_env(env),
+    )
+
+
+def _check_gpus_per_host(
+    host_meshes: HostMeshes, trainer_world_size: int, per_generator_world_size: int
+) -> None:
+    """Fail before spawning anything if the requested GPUs don't fit on the hosts.
+
+    A role's GPUs are split equally across the hosts of its mesh:
+
+        trainer, 4 GPUs, 2-host mesh -> 2 GPUs on each host           OK
+        trainer, 3 GPUs, 2-host mesh -> 1.5 GPUs on each host         fails
+
+    Roles given the same mesh object share its GPUs, trainer first:
+
+        meshes A and B: one host with 4 GPUs each
+        trainer=A (2 GPUs), generators=[A, A, B, B, B, B] (1 GPU each)
+            A: trainer 0,1 | gen0 2 | gen1 3
+            B: gen2 0 | gen3 1 | gen4 2 | gen5 3          OK
+        generators=[A, A, A, B, B, B]
+            A: trainer 0,1 | gen0 2 | gen1 3 | gen2 ?     5 > 4 GPUs: fails
+
+    It has to be the same object: two `this_host()` calls make two meshes, and each
+    starts at GPU 0.
+    """
+    trainer_roles = [("trainer", host_meshes.trainer, trainer_world_size)]
+    generator_roles = [
+        (f"generator{i}", host_mesh, per_generator_world_size)
+        for i, host_mesh in enumerate(host_meshes.generators)
+    ]
+    roles = trainer_roles + generator_roles
+    # For each mesh object (by id), the GPUs per host each of its roles needs.
+    role_gpus_by_mesh: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
+    for role, host_mesh, role_world_size in roles:
+        nodes = len(host_mesh)
+        if role_world_size % nodes != 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{role} world size ({role_world_size}) must be evenly divisible by "
+                f"its host count ({nodes})"
+            )
+        role_gpus_by_mesh.setdefault(id(host_mesh), {})[role] = role_world_size // nodes
+
+    # Check that the roles on each mesh fit in its GPUs per host.
+    for role_gpus in role_gpus_by_mesh.values():
+        total_gpus = sum(role_gpus.values())
+        if total_gpus > host_meshes.gpus_per_node:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Roles on one host mesh need {total_gpus} GPUs per host, but "
+                f"gpus_per_node is {host_meshes.gpus_per_node}: {role_gpus}"
+            )
+
+
+def spawn_proc_mesh(
+    trainer_world_size: int,
+    per_generator_world_size: int,
+    host_meshes: HostMeshes | None = None,
+    *,
+    num_generators: int = 1,
+    generator_env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+) -> tuple[ProcMesh, list[ProcMesh]]:
+    """Spawn the trainer and generator proc meshes.
+
+    Args:
+        trainer_world_size: Number of GPU procs to spawn for the trainer.
+        per_generator_world_size: Number of GPU procs to spawn for each generator.
+        host_meshes: Caller-provided trainer/generator host meshes. When
+            provided, each role is spawned on its provided host mesh; roles given
+            the same host mesh object get non-overlapping GPU ranges on it. None means
+            both roles are spawned on ``this_host()`` by using non-overlapping
+            GPU ranges.
+        num_generators: Number of generator proc meshes to spawn.
+
+    Returns:
+        The ``(trainer_mesh, generator_meshes)`` proc meshes.
+    """
+    total_generator_gpus = num_generators * per_generator_world_size
+    total_gpus = trainer_world_size + total_generator_gpus
+    logger.info(
+        f"{num_generators} generator(s) * {per_generator_world_size} GPUs + "
+        f"{trainer_world_size} trainer GPUs = {total_gpus} total"
+    )
+
+    if host_meshes is not None:
+        trainer_host_mesh = host_meshes.trainer
+        generator_host_meshes = host_meshes.generators
+        gpus_per_node = host_meshes.gpus_per_node
+
+        assert len(generator_host_meshes) == num_generators, (
+            f"expected {num_generators} generator host mesh(es), "
+            f"got {len(generator_host_meshes)}"
+        )
+
+        _check_gpus_per_host(host_meshes, trainer_world_size, per_generator_world_size)
+        # Roles on the same mesh share one provisioner, which hands out the next free GPUs:
+        #   mesh A: trainer -> 0,1 | gen0 -> 2 | gen1 -> 3
+        # Keyed by id(mesh) because a HostMesh can't be a dict key.
+        provisioners: dict[int, PerHostProvisioner] = {}
+        for host_mesh in [trainer_host_mesh, *generator_host_meshes]:
+            provisioners.setdefault(
+                id(host_mesh), PerHostProvisioner(total_gpus=gpus_per_node)
+            )
+        trainer_mesh = _spawn_proc_mesh(
+            trainer_host_mesh,
+            trainer_world_size,
+            provisioners[id(trainer_host_mesh)],
+            bootstrap=_preimport_torch,
+        )
+        generator_meshes = [
+            _spawn_proc_mesh(
+                gen_host_mesh,
+                per_generator_world_size,
+                provisioners[id(gen_host_mesh)],
+                bootstrap=_bootstrap_generator,
+                extra_env=generator_env,
+            )
+            for gen_host_mesh in generator_host_meshes
+        ]
+    else:
+        # Single-node mode: partition GPUs on this_host() via
+        # CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
+        host_mesh = this_host()
+        provisioner = PerHostProvisioner(total_gpus=total_gpus)
+        trainer_mesh = host_mesh.spawn_procs(
+            per_host={"gpus": trainer_world_size},
+            bootstrap=_preimport_torch,
+            bootstrap_command=default_bootstrap_cmd().with_env(
+                provisioner.allocate(trainer_world_size)
+            ),
+        )
+        generator_meshes = [
+            host_mesh.spawn_procs(
+                per_host={"gpus": per_generator_world_size},
+                bootstrap=_bootstrap_generator,
+                bootstrap_command=default_bootstrap_cmd().with_env(
+                    provisioner.allocate(
+                        per_generator_world_size, extra_env=generator_env
+                    )
+                ),
+            )
+            for _ in range(num_generators)
+        ]
+
+    return trainer_mesh, generator_meshes
+
+
+def spawn_cpu_procs(num_procs: int) -> ProcMesh:
+    """Spawn ``num_procs`` CPU procs on the controller host."""
+    return this_host().spawn_procs(per_host={"cpus": num_procs})
+
+
+def shutdown() -> None:
+    """Shut down the Monarch client (normally an atexit hook) and wait for it."""
+    shutdown_context().get()

+"""Monarch's RDMA microbatch for the opt-in RDMA path (`Batcher.Config.rdma_min_tensor_bytes`): the
+batcher registers each microbatch's large tensors as Monarch RDMA buffers, and each trainer rank reads its own
+column.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import ctypes
+import dataclasses
+import logging
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+from monarch.rdma import RDMAAction, RDMABuffer
+from torch.utils import _pytree as pytree
+
+from torchtitan.rl.trainer.batcher import TrainingMicrobatch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class MonarchRDMAMicrobatch:
+    """A `TrainingMicrobatch` whose large tensors stay in its owner, the process that registered it.
+
+    Example:
+        rdma_microbatch = MonarchRDMAMicrobatch.register(  # owner
+            microbatch, min_bytes=1024, batch_index=0, dp_rank=1, microbatch_index=2
+        )
+        microbatch = await rdma_microbatch.read()  # trainer rank: one RDMA action reads every buffer
+        await rdma_microbatch.drop()               # owner, after every rank has read it
+    """
+
+    fields: dict[str, Any]
+    """The microbatch's fields: tensors of at least `min_bytes` (also inside `model_kwargs`) as
+    `_TensorRef`s, the rest by value. Tensors inside a container that pytree can't flatten also go by value."""
+
+    batch_index: int
+    """How many batches the owner registered before this one."""
+
+    dp_rank: int
+    """The trainer DP rank that should read it."""
+
+    microbatch_index: int
+    """Its position in that rank's column."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def register(
+        cls,
+        microbatch: TrainingMicrobatch,
+        *,
+        min_bytes: int,
+        batch_index: int,
+        dp_rank: int,
+        microbatch_index: int,
+    ) -> MonarchRDMAMicrobatch:
+        fields = {
+            field.name: getattr(microbatch, field.name)
+            for field in dataclasses.fields(microbatch)
+        }
+        return cls(
+            fields=pytree.tree_map_only(
+                lambda leaf: (
+                    isinstance(leaf, torch.Tensor) and leaf.nbytes >= min_bytes
+                ),
+                _TensorRef.register,
+                fields,
+            ),
+            batch_index=batch_index,
+            dp_rank=dp_rank,
+            microbatch_index=microbatch_index,
+        )
+
+    async def read(self) -> TrainingMicrobatch:
+        action = RDMAAction()
+
+        def queue_read(tensor_ref: _TensorRef) -> torch.Tensor:
+            # TODO: allocate pinned tensors here. With max_num_documents also set, that removed the
+            # ~4 ms per microbatch in `TrainingEngine._forward_backward_body`'s TODO; pinned alone did not.
+            tensor = torch.empty(tensor_ref.shape, dtype=tensor_ref.dtype)
+            action.read_remote(tensor.view(-1).view(torch.uint8), tensor_ref.buffer)
+            return tensor
+
+        microbatch_fields = pytree.tree_map_only(_TensorRef, queue_read, self.fields)
+        await action.submit()
+        return TrainingMicrobatch(**microbatch_fields)
+
+    async def drop(self) -> None:
+        tensor_refs = [
+            leaf
+            for leaf in pytree.tree_leaves(self.fields)
+            if isinstance(leaf, _TensorRef)
+        ]
+        await asyncio.gather(*(tensor_ref.buffer.drop() for tensor_ref in tensor_refs))
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class _TensorRef:
+    """A tensor as its RDMA buffer, plus the shape and dtype to rebuild it."""
+
+    buffer: RDMABuffer
+    shape: torch.Size
+    dtype: torch.dtype
+
+    @classmethod
+    def register(cls, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> _TensorRef:
+        # A view, not a copy: the buffer keeps the tensor's storage alive until drop().
+        # view(-1) needs a contiguous tensor; the batcher builds only contiguous ones.
+        return cls(
+            buffer=RDMABuffer(tensor.view(-1).view(torch.uint8)),
+            shape=tensor.shape,
+            dtype=tensor.dtype,
+        )
+
+
+# The CUDA driver's `CU_LIMIT_STACK_SIZE` (cuda.h).
+_CU_LIMIT_STACK_SIZE = 0
+
+
+def create_cuda_context_to_silence_monarch_log() -> None:
+    """Make a CUDA context current on GPU 0, so Monarch stops printing `[RdmaXcel] No CUDA context ...`
+    for every registered buffer (its CUDA driver check on each pointer needs a context)."""
+    # TODO: this costs ~256 MiB on GPU 0 (H100). Remove it when Monarch prints this line once, not per
+    # buffer (https://github.com/meta-pytorch/monarch/issues/5049; per buffer in torchmonarch 0.7.0).
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.cuda is None:
+        return
+    try:
+        torch.zeros(1, device="cuda")
+    except RuntimeError as error:  # e.g. GPU 0 is full or in exclusive-process mode
+        logger.warning(
+            f"No CUDA context, so Monarch logs one line per RDMA buffer: {error}"
+        )
+        return
+    # The driver raises the stack limit when a kernel needs more, so 0 halves the context (520 -> 256 MiB).
+    ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1").cuCtxSetLimit(_CU_LIMIT_STACK_SIZE, ctypes.c_size_t(0))

I kept these, because the pool is an implementation detail of the default `Rollouter`: `VerifiersRollouter` runs rollouts in its Verifiers EnvServer and spawns no pool. If the controller spawned the pool and passed it in, it would spawn processes the Verifiers rollouter never uses, or need a "does this rollouter want a pool" flag. While checking this I found that `VerifiersRollouter.setup_async` did not take `actor_system`, so the verifiers recipes would have failed. Fixed, with a test that its signature matches `Rollouter.setup_async`. Happy to switch to a controller-owned pool if you prefer it.

@tianyu-l one concern before this merges: launchers that bring their own hosts.

1. On main, `Controller.setup_async(trainer_mesh=..., generator_meshes=...)` lets a launcher allocate hosts itself and hand the controller ready proc meshes.
2. FairTitan's Slurm launcher depends on that. It loads host meshes from its Slurm allocation, calls `spawn_proc_mesh(..., host_meshes=host_meshes, generator_env=...)`, and passes the result to `setup_async`: [launcher/rl/main.py#L49-L60](https://github.com/fairinternal/fairtitan/blob/46a9a467ed6d2524910ba98b0081a8789e6ae947/launcher/rl/main.py#L49-L60) (internal repo).

Could `MonarchActorSystem` keep a way to take caller-provided `HostMeshes`, for example a constructor argument or an overridable `provision`? Happy to send it as a follow-up if you'd rather land this as is.

```python
actor_system = config.actor_system.build(host_meshes=host_meshes, generator_env=generator_env)
await controller.setup_async(actor_system=actor_system)
```
